A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AVFakeBench research work, with readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. All 23 pages were compared; pages 4–23 are textually and visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 AV-LMMs and two expert detectors in Section 4, including quantitative results in Tables 3–5 and case studies in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v3 retains those original quantitative evaluations in Section 4 and qualitative case studies in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The synthesis and editing pipelines, modality combinations, and annotation procedure in Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same data sources and 3,000 clips covering human and general subjects, 11 scenarios, seven audio-video combinations, and four evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 and Tables 3–5 retain the same comparator membership: 11 AV-LMMs, with LipFD and AVH-Align additionally evaluated for binary judgment.

E3.justification: Sample counts, task definitions, answer parsing, accuracy and macro-F1 reporting, and GPT-based explanation scoring remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1.

E4.justification: The forgery-state breakdown, model-bias and modality-disparity analyses, and Appendix B.2 case studies are identical. No ablations or robustness analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 3 gives Gemini-2.5-pro the same overall binary F1 of 59.9% and forgery-classification F1 of 19.2% in both versions.

T1.justification: The forgery taxonomy and mathematical definitions are unchanged, including the Normalized Bias Index in Appendix B.1, Equation (1). No proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and construction-framework contributions and claims about AV-LMMs' potential and fine-grained detection and reasoning weaknesses.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning face-centric detector failures, prediction bias, modality imbalance, and explanatory limitations remain identical in Sections 4.2–4.3 and the appendix case studies.

D1.justification: Data-selection criteria, generation and annotation prompts, human-verification procedures, and evaluation details are unchanged. The added author email line supplies general correspondence information without new code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the bibliography are unchanged. The benchmark's positioning relative to prior datasets and multimodal models is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a corresponding-author and email line beneath the affiliations. Apart from this and the arXiv version/date stamp, the wording, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added correspondence line shifts Figure 1 downward and causes text reflow across pages 1–3. Figure and table content is unchanged, and pages 4–23 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 adds author contact information and makes small accompanying layout shifts. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
